mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility raises weekday trip chaining into shops and restaurants, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved from t-3w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC also moved upward
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for four weeks but RETAIL_REC is still lower than in the prior four-week window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility declines below its recent level, more time spent outside home translates into more discretionary retail visits, pushing RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point week-on-week from its recent average
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.4 at t-3w to 16.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls further but RETAIL_REC does not rise within the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between rising GROCERY_PHARM and rising TRANSIT indicates more multi-purpose trips, which spills over into retail-and-recreation visits and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT are both less negative at t-0w than at t-3w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both improve together but RETAIL_REC fails to outperform its prior four-week mean, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains heavily depressed, access friction suppresses casual shopping trips and RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next week than over the last week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 for a full week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is still at -55.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -50 for a week and RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises over the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary time toward outdoor recreation, which reduces retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 55.3 at t-3w and 40.3 at t-0w, still far above baseline
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated or rises further but RETAIL_REC is higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both weaken at the same time, routine local trip demand softens and retail outings follow down within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES drifted from -49.3 to -45.3 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed near -17
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both continue to weaken together but RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES translate into more in-person access and lunchtime retail demand, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved steadily across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep improving in a reopening regime but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebounds sharply after being below its recent peak, the rebound signals renewed leisure activity that spills into nearby shops and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week after a prior two-week decline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 55.3 at t-3w to 27.1 at t-1w, then rebounded to 40.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS makes a similar rebound but RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
